applied.problem: Over-general and over-certain: 'A battery' has milliohms and drives thousands of amps only if large (bold drops 'large'); 'takes no part in the reaction' overstates the quote ('isn't used'); 3.60 V is one lithium-ion type, not all; a battery that gives out early on test is beyond the 60% data.

Electrolyte line is false for lithium-ion, just taught; '60% gives over 90%' is stated as general where the source is one test series; breaking capacity should be 'at least' and DC-rated, as screen 0 and BS 7671 put it; '12 V drives over a thousand amps' holds only for a large battery; insulated tools are standard safe practice.

Screen 9 states one test's 5 to 10 ms as a general law; screens 11 and 14 treat 3.60 V as every lithium-ion cell; screen 12 says KOH 'takes no part' where the source says it is not used up; screen 2's 1800 A ignores spanner and contact resistance; screen 7's 'cannot run its load for long' goes beyond the 60% data.
